content:
Vice President JD Vance is turned into a turkey in a scathing new Thanksgiving-themed ad released by the Democratic super PAC Priorities USA.

Donald Trump, meanwhile, becomes the face of a butternut squash, Secretary of State Marco Rubio a russet potato and outgoing Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis a sweet potato in the spot targeting Republicans over affordability.

The ad, titled “Talking Turkey,” opens with a woman preparing Thanksgiving dinner.

“I’m going to give my family the holiday they deserve, no matter what it costs,” she says, before glancing at her grocery receipt and uttering, “Oh, shit,” at the prices she’s paid.

She then picks up the squash, onto which Trump’s face is superimposed, and President Butternut dismisses the affordability crisis as a “con job.”

Rubio, in sweet potato form, suggests Americans should consider themselves fortunate given gas prices elsewhere in the world.

And Vance, whose face appears on an uncooked turkey, declares: “Prices are going to come down, but it’s going to take a little bit of time.”

“That turkey’s a liar,” the woman responds.

As the talking vegetables and turkey continue to spout Republican rhetoric, the exasperated woman shoves turkey Vance into the oven to silence him.

“Republican talk is cheap. Turkey isn’t,” a voiceover declares.

“Dig in, we’ve got two more years,” the woman tells her family.

The 60-second spot was launched Monday and will run on social media and streaming TV platforms in Michigan, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, North Carolina, Georgia and Arizona.

“Cost of living was the defining issue of the midterms, and Republicans spent the cycle insisting prices were coming down,” said Danielle Butterfield, the president of Priorities USA, in a press release.

“Families are feeling the pain of this economy as they celebrate the holidays, and we’re using this moment to remind them who got us here in the first place,” Butterfield added. “We need to ensure that whoever emerges from the 2028 Republican primary carries the weight of the Trump Administration’s economic record, and Priorities is making sure voters connect Republican presidential contenders to that record now, before any of them can run from it.”

Priorities USA is spending $30 million against potential GOP presidential candidates ahead of the 2028 election.

CORRECTION: A previous version of this article swapped the types of potatoes used to portray Gov. Ron DeSantis and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
